title: Glyph Grids, Cut Corners, Scroll Shred, State Orbs & Exploded Layers
description: Five effects driven by a measurement instead of a timeline: luminance, corner specs, scroll velocity, envelopes and computed styles.

drops.title: Live ASCII Renderer
drops.description: Three procedural scenes sampled to a luminance grid and printed as characters — no canvas, no images.
drops.concept: Animated ASCII is having a moment again, and the mechanism is simpler than it looks: render or compute a scene, reduce each cell to a brightness, index a character ramp. This drop runs a z-buffered torus, an additive plasma and a height-field sea side by side off one frame loop, with live density, frame-rate and ramp controls so the separation between geometry and glyph is obvious.
drops.source: bas3line/ascii — animated ASCII art for web pages

interaction.mouse: Drag the density and frame-rate sliders; switch the character ramp.
interaction.click: Toggle invert to flip the brightness mapping.
interaction.touch: All controls are plain inputs and work on touch.

drops.title: Native Frame Shapes
drops.description: Bevels, notches, scoops and squircles on any single vertex, with a stroke that follows the geometry.
drops.concept: Shaped panels usually cheat with a background image or a pseudo-element wedge, which breaks the moment you want a border. Generating a clip-path: shape() per corner and painting the box twice — full size in the stroke colour, inset by the stroke width in the surface colour — gives a genuinely shaped box with a genuine border. The declarative corner-shape property sits alongside for the cases where one family per box is enough.
drops.source: kodecagency/ns-frame — native shapes compiled to CSS shape()

interaction.mouse: Tune corner size and stroke width; override the shape or the corner set.
interaction.click: Pick a shape family from the override menu to apply it to every panel.
interaction.touch: Sliders and selects are touch-sized; the bento reflows to two columns.

drops.title: Scroll Speed Scramble
drops.description: Headlines that fall apart in proportion to how fast you scroll and resolve the moment you stop.
drops.concept: Scroll distance per frame is smoothed into an energy value, and every character rolls a die against it — weighted so the outer letters tear first and the line reads as breaking apart. Because the energy is a decaying filter rather than a timer, the settle is free: at zero velocity every roll fails and the real text is simply what remains.

interaction.mouse: Scroll — fast flicks shred, slow drags barely disturb the letters.
interaction.click: Adjust sensitivity, settle rate and character set in the panel.
interaction.touch: Flick-scrolling gives the strongest effect; the panel docks to the bottom.

drops.title: Agent State Orbs
drops.description: One particle sphere that reads as resting, listening, thinking or answering — no second widget required.
drops.concept: Assistant UIs keep inventing a new indicator per state. A single point cloud carries all four if each state changes something structural: rest breathes, listen couples the radius to an input envelope, think contracts the cloud and sweeps a bright band around its latitudes, and speak ejects particles on syllable onsets so output never looks like input. Envelopes are synthesised, so nothing asks for a microphone.
drops.source: aqualang89/shipnotes-components — particle orbs that listen, think and talk

interaction.mouse: Hover to tilt an orb; move across it to steer the spin axis.
interaction.click: Click an orb to cycle its state, or pick a state from the buttons.
interaction.touch: Tap to cycle; auto-cycle runs all four states until you intervene.

drops.title: Exploded Component
drops.description: A live card pulled apart into six paint layers, with redlines read off the DOM rather than typed.
drops.concept: Component documentation drifts because the numbers in it are copies. Here each layer of the isometric figure is a clone of the running component with the other layers' paint made transparent, every measurement comes from getComputedStyle, and the interactive states are forced through the component's own declarations rather than re-described. Press T and raw pixel values swap for the custom-property names the author actually wrote.
drops.source: diip3sh/exploded — explode a live component into paint layers

interaction.mouse: Hover a layer or a list row to select it and read its redlines.
interaction.click: Click the figure to collapse or explode the stack; switch the forced state.
interaction.touch: Tap the figure to toggle; the layer list and state switcher are tap targets.
